questions.question: Which command records a test and generates Python code?
options: `npx playwright codegen --lang=python`
`npx playwright codegen --target=python`
`npx playwright test --codegen=python`
`npx playwright record --python`
questions.explanation: Codegen chooses its output language with `--target`. It has no `--lang` option.

questions.question: A generated test ends with `await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click();`. What is the main problem?
options: `getByRole` is too fragile for generated code
The click needs a fixed wait before it
It never checks that submitting worked
It must be wrapped in `try`/`catch`
questions.explanation: Without an assertion on the outcome, the test passes even when the form does nothing.

questions.question: What happens with `page.waitForFunction(fn, { timeout: 5000 })`?
options: The object is passed to `fn`, and the timeout is ignored
It waits for up to 5 seconds
TypeScript and the runtime both reject the call
It polls `fn` every 5 seconds
questions.explanation: The second parameter is the argument for `fn`. Options go third: `waitForFunction(fn, undefined, { timeout: 5000 })`.

questions.question: When is `expect(async () => { ... }).toPass()` the right choice?
options: Whenever one element needs time to appear
To make a whole test retry in CI
To replace every web-first assertion
When several steps must be repeated together until they succeed
questions.explanation: A single web-first assertion already retries. `toPass` is for a block, such as clicking refresh and then checking the result.

questions.question: A test catches a failed link click and calls `page.goto('/sweets')` instead. What is the risk?
options: `page.goto()` can't be called inside `catch`
The test stays green even when the link is broken for users
The browser context closes after the failed click
The test will always time out
questions.explanation: The fallback reaches the page by another route, so the behaviour the test was meant to prove is no longer tested.
